problems: stop 1 card 4, answer 2: copies a Prep line word for word
stop 1 card 14, answer 2: a reaction phrase

explanations.explanation: Yes. David says, "I shall not want," and that means he will not lack what he needs because the LORD is his shepherd. That is a steady kind of care. Not a crumb missed.

Not this one. David is not talking about earning anything here. He says, "The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want," so the idea is lack, not paychecks or hustle. He is being cared for, not clocking in.
That is not the line here. David says he shall not want in Psalm 23:1, which means he will not lack what he needs. The picture is shepherd care, not things slipping away. The LORD is enough.

Yes, baker. Green pastures and quiet waters sound like rest and peace, and that is exactly the picture David paints in Psalm 23:2. The shepherd is not rushing the sheep around. He is giving them a calm place to lie down.
No, not here. David says the LORD makes him lie down in green pastures and leads him beside quiet waters in Psalm 23:2. That is not a hustle scene. That is rest.
That is not the picture in this verse. David talks about green pastures and quiet waters, which gives a calm feel in Psalm 23:2. The danger comes later in the song. Here, the sheep can breathe.
Right. David says, "He restores my soul" in Psalm 23:3. The LORD's care does not stop at the outside of the sheep. It reaches all the way in.
Not in this verse. David says the LORD "restores my soul" in Psalm 23:3. That is healing and renewal, not a test. The shepherd is mending, not grading.
No. Psalm 23:3 says, "He restores my soul." David is talking about the LORD bringing him back, not weighing him down or measuring him out. That is grace with both hands.

explanations.answer: For the sake of His name
explanations.explanation: Yes. David says the LORD guides him in the paths of righteousness "for the sake of His name" in Psalm 23:3. That means the LORD's own name is honored in the way He leads. The shepherd is faithful to who He is.

explanations.answer: For the sake of His flock
explanations.explanation: That is not what David says here. Psalm 23:3 says the LORD guides him in the paths of righteousness "for the sake of His name." The reason given is the LORD's name, not the flock's. He leads with His own glory in view.

explanations.answer: For the sake of His land
explanations.explanation: No, baker. David does not say that in Psalm 23:3. He says the LORD guides him in righteousness for the sake of His name. The focus is on the LORD's name, not the land.

explanations.answer: Because the LORD is with him
explanations.explanation: Right. David says, "I will fear no evil, for You are with me" in Psalm 23:4. That is the reason he gives. The valley is dark, but he is not alone.

No. David does not say he can handle it by himself. In Psalm 23:4, he says, "for You are with me." The comfort comes from the LORD's presence, not David's toughness. That is a different kind of courage.
That is not David's reason in Psalm 23:4. He says he will fear no evil because the LORD is with him. The verse does not lean on the length of the valley. It leans on the nearness of the LORD.
Yes, that is true. David says the LORD's rod and staff comfort him in Psalm 23:4. Even in the valley of the shadow of death, the shepherd's care is not gone. It comforts him there.
No, that is not what David says. In Psalm 23:4 he says, "Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me." The valley is dark, but the shepherd's tools are still a comfort. David says it plainly.
Yes. David says, "You prepare a table before me" in Psalm 23:5. The LORD is pictured as the host setting out a place for him. That is generous care.
Not this picture. Psalm 23:5 says the LORD prepares a table before David. The verse does not mention a tent. It is a host and guest scene.
No, baker. David says the LORD prepares a table in Psalm 23:5. That is a meal image, not a bed image. The LORD is welcoming him, not putting him down for the night.

No, that one misses the verse. David says the LORD prepares a table "in the presence of my enemies" in Psalm 23:5, not far away from them. The point is not distance. The point is the LORD's care right there in view of them.
Baked just right. David says the LORD prepares the table "in the presence of my enemies" in Psalm 23:5. So it is not far away from them. The verse puts the table right where they can see it.
Yes. A cup that overflows is a picture of more than enough in Psalm 23:5. David is saying the LORD's provision is abundant. Not just enough. Overflowing.
No, that is not the picture. When David says his cup overflows in Psalm 23:5, he is talking about abundance. It is the kind of fullness that spills over because there is so much. Not carelessness.
No. Psalm 23:5 is not about being hurried along. David says, "my cup overflows," which paints a picture of plenty. The LORD is not rushing him. He is blessing him richly.
Yes. David says, "Surely goodness and mercy will follow me all the days of my life" in Psalm 23:6. Those are the two things named in the verse. They are staying with him all the way.

That is not what David says here. Psalm 23:6 says goodness and mercy will follow him all the days of his life. Wealth and honor are not the words of the verse. David is talking about the LORD's kindness.
No, baker. David names goodness and mercy in Psalm 23:6. Those are the ones that follow him all the days of his life. The verse does not say strength and wisdom here.

explanations.answer: In the house of the LORD
explanations.explanation: Yes. David says he will dwell "in the house of the LORD forever" in Psalm 23:6. That is where the song lands. After all the paths and valleys, he ends at home with the LORD.
Not here. David closes Psalm 23:6 by saying he will dwell in the house of the LORD forever. Hebron is not the place named in this verse. The song ends with the LORD's house.
No, baker. Psalm 23:6 says David will dwell "in the house of the LORD forever." That is the place the verse names. The song closes with the LORD's house, not the land of Canaan.
